people.name: Baruch
people.description: Scribe who wrote the book in Babylon and read it to the exiles.
people.identity_note: Baruch son of Neriah son of Mahseiah matches Jeremiah 32:12; Baruch 1:1 extends the line three generations further.

people.name: Nerias
people.description: Father of Baruch.

people.name: Maaseas
people.description: Grandfather of Baruch.

people.name: Sedekias
people.description: Great-grandfather of Baruch, son of Asadias.
people.identity_note: Distinct from King Sedekias son of Josias (1:8).

people.name: Asadias
people.description: Ancestor of Baruch, son of Helkias.
people.identity_note: Not the existing 'hasadiah' (a post-exilic descendant of Jehoiachin, 1 Chr 3:20).

people.name: Helkias
people.description: Earliest named ancestor of Baruch.
people.identity_note: Not identifiable with any Hebrew-Bible Hilkiah; distinct from Helkias father of the high priest Joakim (1:7).

people.name: Jechonias
people.description: Exiled king of Judah who heard Baruch's reading in Babylon.

people.name: Joakim
people.description: King of Judah, father of Jechonias.

people.name: Joakim
people.description: High priest in Jerusalem to whom the exiles sent money.
people.identity_note: Absent from the Hebrew Bible's high-priest lists (Seraiah was high priest at the fall, 2 Ki 25:18); unrelated to Joiakim son of Jeshua (Neh 12:10).

people.name: Helkias
people.description: Father of the high priest Joakim, son of Salom.
people.identity_note: 'Hilkiah son of Shallum' matches the high priest Hilkiah son of Shallum (existing 'hilkiah-2ki22', 1 Chr 6:13), but that genealogy gives him no son Joakim; possible identity flagged, not mapped.

people.name: Salom
people.description: Grandfather of the high priest Joakim.
people.identity_note: Possibly = Shallum the high priest (existing 'shallum-1ch6'); not mapped, see the Helkias (1:7) note.

people.name: Sedekias
people.description: King of Judah who had silver temple vessels made.

people.name: Josias
people.description: King of Judah, father of Sedekias.

people.name: Nabuchodonosor
people.description: King of Babylon who exiled Jechonias.
people.identity_note: 6:1 'the king of the Babylonians' is named in 6:2.

people.name: Baltasar
people.description: Son of Nabuchodonosor for whose life the exiles are to pray.
people.identity_note: The text calls him Nebuchadnezzar's son (as Daniel 5 does); historically he was son of Nabonidus, as the existing 'belshazzar' description says. Parent link recorded as stated; reviewer may treat it as dynastic.

people.name: Moses
people.description: Lawgiver through whom the curse and the law were given.

people.name: Abraham
people.description: Patriarch to whom the land was promised.

people.name: Isaac
people.description: Patriarch to whom the land was promised.

people.name: Jacob
people.description: Patriarch to whom the land was promised.
people.identity_note: 'Jacob' in 3:36 and 4:2 denotes the people and is not counted.

people.name: Jeremy
people.description: Prophet credited with the letter to the exiles (Letter of Jeremiah, ch.6).

excluded_names.Agar: eponym for a people ('sons of Agar' 3:23), not the person Hagar

notes: Baruch 1:1 genealogy: Baruch < Nerias < Maaseas < Sedekias < Asadias < Helkias, recorded as a parent chain; Baruch/Nerias/Maaseas mapped to existing baruch-jer32 / neriah / mahseiah (Jer 32:12). Ch.1 has two different Helkias, two Sedekias and two Joakims; parent links carry 'new_id' or 'existing_id' to disambiguate. Chapter 6 = Letter of Jeremiah (6:1-73); only Jeremy and Nabuchodonosor are named people there. Oddities: 1:2 'fifth year' after the burning of Jerusalem with Baruch in Babylon (Jeremiah 43 places him in Egypt); 1:8 has vessels made by Sedekias returned after Jechonias's exile; 1:11 Baltasar as son of Nebuchadnezzar.
